newsitem.title: USA: West African crudes pry into U.S. Gulf, arb tight.
newsitem.headline: West African crudes pry into U.S. Gulf, arb tight.

text.p: U.S. refinery demand improved modestly Thursday amid a still-soft margin climate and a prohibitive trans-Atlantic arbitrage into the U.S.
Several West African crude shipments were reported traded into the Gulf Coast overnight for second-half October, with Brent also rumored done at a relatively high price.
Prompt Cabinda and late October Escravos were reported traded into the U.S. Gulf on Wednesday, with early Oct Brent heard moved at WTI plus 10 cents cif.
Cabinda was seen sold at Dated Brent -$1.10 fob to a U.S. refiner, with another parcel done at WTI minus 60 cents cif.
A refiner also sold Escravos around Dated Brent plus 46 cents fob to two different buyers.
"Some refiners will take distillate-rich crudes because of their yield," a trader said, but added that profits were slim with premiums for light grades some 50-70 cents over WTI.
Within the region, Chile's ENAP purchased 985,000 barrels of Palanca and 400,000 barrels of Oriente for early Nov, but price levels were not immediately available.
Oct Oriente was assessed doable at WTI minus $1.85-90 cif, with Oct Cusiana pegged at WTI minus five cents fob.
In the U.S. aftermarket, Nov Brent drifted about five cents down from the IPE close to $22.87-89 a barrel.
Intermonth Oct/Nov Brent traded at 40 cents, and Nov/Dec moved at 50 cents, moderately weaker than the London session.
